name: Mark Pears
current_role: Chief Executive, William Pears Group (since 1984); Chairman, Talisman Global Asset Management; trustee, Pears Foundation
profile: London property billionaire who has run the family's privately held William Pears Group, founded in 1952 by his grandfather Bernard and father Clive, since his father's death in 1984 when he was 21. He runs it with brothers Trevor and David; together they co-founded Pears Foundation (1992), one of the UK's largest family foundations.
interesting_fact: Appointed CBE in 2014 'for services to Business and to Charity'; he has been a trustee of the British Museum and the homelessness charity St Mungo's.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000 he co-founded Telereal, which became the UK's largest property outsourcing company, managing estates for British Telecom, the DWP, the DVLA and Royal Mail assets.
notes: Low public profile; family business is private. Foundation is invitation-only and asks not to receive funding requests; general foundation inbox is the only published route found.

name: Leopoldo Del Pino Y Calvo Sotelo
current_role: Private investor; major Ferrovial shareholder via his holding company Siemprelara (Ferrovial director 2010-2016)
profile: One of the children of Rafael del Pino y Moreno, who founded construction and infrastructure group Ferrovial in 1952; brother of Ferrovial chairman Rafael del Pino. He sat on Ferrovial's board from 2010 to early 2016 and has gradually sold down a stake that once exceeded 8%, investing through his vehicle Siemprelara and SICAVs.
interesting_fact: His Ferrovial shares came from the family holding Portman Baela, which distributed 40.82% of Ferrovial's capital directly to the siblings' individual vehicles, his being Siemprelara.
deep_cut_fact: Through Siemprelara he created and presides over the Fundación Estrella de los Mares, whose stated aims include promoting Spanish history, including its famous navigators.
notes: Very private; no personal site or social accounts found. MarketScreener lists him as a director of the Spanish parking association (Asociacion Espanola de Aparcamientos y Garajes). The foundation is the only possible route but no published contact was found.

name: Brijmohan Lall Munjal
profile: Founder of the Hero Group / Hero MotoCorp (motorcycles); died 1 November 2015 in New Delhi, aged 92.
notes: Deceased 1 Nov 2015 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brijmohan_Lall_Munjal ; https://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/hero-founder-brijmohan-lall-munjal-passes-away-9597). Son Pawan Munjal leads Hero MotoCorp.

name: Ziff, Dirk, Robert And Daniel
current_role: Co-founders/principals of Ziff Brothers Investments, the family's private investment office
profile: The three sons of publisher William B. Ziff Jr. inherited their fortune after the family sold most of Ziff-Davis/Ziff Communications in 1994 (a 1998 joint Forbes listing). They formed Ziff Brothers Investments, a famously discreet family office investing across equities, debt, real estate, commodities, private equity and hedge funds; they now are listed individually.
interesting_fact: Ziff Brothers Investments provided early seed capital to Daniel Och's hedge fund, which became Och-Ziff Capital Management and went public in 2007 (Wikipedia flags this as needing a citation).
deep_cut_fact: Robert Ziff studied electrical and computer engineering at Harvard (magna cum laude), graduated first in his class at Cornell Law School where he edited the Cornell Law Review, and in 2008 endowed the Robert D. Ziff Professorship of Law at Cornell. Dirk and Daniel gave $2m in 2018 to Columbia's Center for Climate and Life.
notes: Family/group entry (1998 Forbes list) covering three brothers; each is now profiled separately. Very private family office with no public website or published contact; outreach would need a warm intro.

name: Juan March Delgado
current_role: President of the board of trustees, Fundación Juan March (and of the Instituto Juan March)
profile: Grandson of Juan March Ordinas, who founded Banca March in Palma de Mallorca in 1926. With his brother Carlos he controls Banca March, Spain's only 100% family-owned bank, and a large stake in investment group Corporación Financiera Alba, which he co-chaired until 2018. He left the Banca March board in 2021 after 27 years and now focuses on the family foundation, which is arts-focused.
interesting_fact: He sat on Banca March's board from 1994 until July 2021, when his daughter Catalina March Juan took his seat as part of a planned handover to the family's next generation.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Palma de Mallorca in 1940, he is a trained engineer, holding a Doctorate in Industrial Engineering from Madrid's Universidad Politécnica.
notes: Aged about 86 and private. The best route is via Fundación Juan March (Madrid); march.es blocked automated fetching, so its press/contact page could not be checked. Note: Juan March de la Lastra (a different person, a cousin's line) chairs Banca March and Alba.

name: Daniel Pritzker
current_role: Musician/filmmaker; president and director, Jay Pritzker Foundation
profile: Son of Hyatt co-founder Jay Pritzker and one of the Chicago Pritzker family's billionaire heirs (Hyatt and family investments). Rather than run the business, he became a musician and filmmaker: he founded the band Sonia Dada and wrote and directed films on jazz pioneers, including Louis (2010) and Bolden (2019), which he self-funded over more than a decade.
interesting_fact: He bought Jerry Garcia's 'Wolf' guitar for $790,000 in 2002 and put it up for a 2017 charity auction. The sale raised $3.2 million for the Southern Poverty Law Center.
deep_cut_fact: He formed Sonia Dada in Chicago in 1990 after hearing three singers performing in a subway station. Their 1992 single 'You Don't Treat Me No Good' spent four weeks at No. 1 in Australia and was the third-best-selling single there in 1993.
notes: No personal social accounts or published email found. The Jay Pritzker Foundation (Tufts BA 1981, Northwestern JD 1986; the foundation funded the $10m Pritzker Challenge at Tufts) is invitation-only. The band site/Facebook (facebook.com/soniadadaband) is the only public channel tied to him.

name: the Leventis family
current_role: Family group: controlling shareholders (with the David family) of Coca-Cola HBC via Kar-Tess Holding; Leventis Group; A. G. Leventis Foundation (chaired by Anastasios Paul Leventis)
profile: Greek-Cypriot dynasty founded by Anastasios G. Leventis, whose West African trading house A. G. Leventis & Co. (1936) grew into a Nigerian/Ghanaian conglomerate. From the 1970s, Constantine Leventis expanded the family's soft-drinks business into Europe; the Hellenic Bottling Company merged with Coca-Cola Beverages to form Coca-Cola HBC, its main source of wealth today. Media assets come from relative Alki David.
interesting_fact: In the 1948 Accra riots, the most serious anti-colonial violence in post-war West Africa, the only large stores left unburned were those of A. G. Leventis & Co.
deep_cut_fact: Founder Anastasios G. Leventis was born in 1902 in the Cypriot mountain village of Lemythou, studied commerce in Bordeaux, and started out in 1920 as a manager for an Anglo-Hellenic firm in south-eastern Nigeria. In 2025 the family's foundation partnered with the Coca-Cola HBC Foundation on a EUR1m programme to restore fire-hit areas of Limassol.
notes: Multi-person family entry (Sunday Times 2020, shared with Alki David). For outreach, pick a specific member, e.g. Anastasios I. Leventis (Coca-Cola HBC non-exec director) or Anastasios P. Leventis (foundation chair). The CCHBC press office is the corporate route. Alive status is per-member, so it is left as 'unknown'.

name: Arvindkumar Poddar
current_role: CEO & Managing Director (chairman & MD in earlier filings), Balkrishna Industries Ltd (BKT Tires), Mumbai
profile: Arvind Poddar controls and runs Balkrishna Industries (BKT), the Mumbai-listed maker of off-highway tyres for agriculture, mining and earthmoving. BKT opened its first off-highway tyre plant in Aurangabad in 1987 and sells mainly into replacement markets in Europe and North America. It held about 8% of the global off-the-road tyre segment in 2014 and supplies OEMs such as JCB, John Deere and CNH.
interesting_fact: Under Poddar, BKT became a major sports sponsor: the official tyre of Monster Jam since 2014 and title sponsor of Italy's Serie BKT and France's Ligue 2 BKT (extended to 2028). In October 2026 it announced a 50:50 joint venture with Pirelli to make Pirelli-branded premium tyres in India.
notes: Web search budget ran out at this point, so research came from Wikipedia and BKT's site only and no sourced deep-cut fact was found. BKT runs a registration-only Press Hub for journalists, which is the logical route. The investor-relations email is in stock-exchange filings but was not verified here.

name: Adani Vinodbhai Shantilal
current_role: Head of a Dubai-based family investment office (Excel Investment and Advisory Services; Adani Global Investment DMCC)
profile: Vinod Adani, born in Gujarat in 1949, is the elder brother of Gautam Adani. He has lived in Dubai since 1994 and holds Cypriot citizenship. He began in the family commodity trading business, founded VR Textile in Mumbai in 1976, traded commodities from Singapore from 1989, and helped finance the Adani group's early projects, including Mundra Port. He now runs a family investment office in Dubai.
interesting_fact: Forbes estimated his net worth at $16.4 billion in 2025, far above this list's older $2.9bn Hurun figure. He has also used the name Vinod Shantilal Shah since 1996.
deep_cut_fact: He founded his first business, VR Textile, in Mumbai in 1976, then moved to Singapore in 1989 to trade commodities before relocating to Dubai in 1994.
notes: Very private, with no public website, social accounts or published contact. He is the subject of regulatory and media controversy (Hindenburg 2023, SEBI 2024); the journalist should be aware before reaching out. Any approach would likely go via the Adani Group's corporate communications.

name: Gudrun Heine
current_role: Co-owner (about 44%) of Karl Storz SE & Co. KG, Tuttlingen; not in an executive role
profile: Daughter of Karl Storz, who founded the endoscopy company in Tuttlingen in 1945 to make ENT instruments and lamps. The company pioneered 'cold light' illumination (1960) and the rod-lens system (1965), which helped create modern endoscopy. It is privately held, with about EUR2.2bn revenue in 2023 and roughly 9,800 staff. She and her sister Sybill each own about 44%; Sybill's son Karl-Christian runs it.
interesting_fact: Karl Storz's 'cold light illumination', bringing bright light from an external source into the body via a flexible fibre-optic cable, laid the groundwork for modern endoscopy; the firm now has more than 15,000 products for human, veterinary and industrial use.
notes: Extremely low public profile. Almost no public information exists about her personally; her sister Sybill Storz was the public face. Only the corporate press inbox is available. Web search budget was exhausted, so research came from Wikipedia and the company site only.

name: Huang Xiaofen
current_role: Director and major shareholder, Shenzhen Kinwong Electronics Co. (SSE: 603228)
profile: Co-owner, with her husband and chairman Liu Shaobo, of Kinwong Electronics, a Shenzhen printed-circuit-board maker founded in 1993 that grew out of a joint venture with a state-owned company. Kinwong supplies rigid, flexible, metal-base, HDI and RF boards for automotive, telecom, servers and consumer electronics, and listed in Shanghai in 2017.
interesting_fact: Kinwong started in 1993 in Shenzhen's Nanshan District. Its first Jiangxi plant (2014) was designed to be more than 70% automated, and its PCBs now go into server/computing and automotive applications.
notes: Low personal profile, with no interviews found. Her husband Liu Shaobo is the company's public face. The company's server-PCB business is relevant to the data-center theme. Research was limited because the web search budget was exhausted.

name: Luo Tsai-Ren
current_role: Vice Chairman, Cheng Shin Rubber Industry Co. (Maxxis/CST tyres; TWSE: 2105), since May 2023
profile: Lo Tsai-jen (b. 1953, Changhua, Taiwan) is the second son of Luo Jye, who founded Cheng Shin Rubber in Yuanlin in 1967 as a bicycle-tyre maker; it grew into Maxxis, one of the world's largest tyre groups. He built and ran its mainland China operations, chaired the group from 2014 to 2020, and returned as vice chairman in 2023.
interesting_fact: He succeeded his father as chairman of Cheng Shin on 17 June 2014 and stepped down in June 2020, when former general manager Chen Rong-hua took over. He returned to the board as vice chairman in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He studied marketing and materials management at New Jersey Institute of Technology (entering 1972). In 1993 he was sent to Kunshan to build Cheng Shin's China plant. A 2014 Business Today profile was headlined that he 'doesn't like socialising' and 'made the factory his home for twenty years'.
notes: Taiwanese, though listed under China. Low-key and reportedly shuns socialising. No personal channels or published press contact found; CST/Maxxis corporate is the only route. Research was limited because the web search budget was exhausted.

name: Greg Mondre
current_role: Managing Partner and Co-Chairman, Silver Lake (previously Co-CEO), per the firm's current bio
profile: Technology private-equity investor who joined Silver Lake in 1999 after time as a principal at TPG (Texas Pacific Group) and as an investment banker in Goldman Sachs' Communications, Media & Entertainment group. He rose to co-lead the roughly $100bn firm, working on deals including Motorola Solutions, GoDaddy, GoodRx, Red Ventures and Expedia. His wealth comes from his Silver Lake partnership stake.
interesting_fact: Directly relevant to the data-center theme: he sits on the board of Vantage Data Centers North America, alongside Fanatics, Equinox, GoodRx, Red Ventures, Relativity, A Place for Mom and Imagine Learning.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.S. in Economics from Wharton. Before private equity he was an investment banker in Goldman Sachs' Communications, Media and Entertainment Group, and early boards he sat on included Network General and UGS Corporation.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center episode via Vantage Data Centers. No published personal contacts; the route is Silver Lake's media relations. Silver Lake's site blocks automated fetching, so the press contact could not be verified. His title appears to have changed from Co-CEO to Co-Chairman; confirm before outreach.

name: Tomas Chrenek Sr
current_role: Controlling owner, AGEL healthcare group; major shareholder, Moravia Steel
profile: Slovak-born, self-made industrialist (age 63, based in Prague) who built his fortune in steel and healthcare. He is a major shareholder in Czech steel trader/producer Moravia Steel (linked to the Třinec steelworks) and controls AGEL, one of Central Europe's largest private hospital and healthcare groups, operating in the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
interesting_fact: He serves as Honorary Consul of Costa Rica in Slovakia.
deep_cut_fact: Forbes notes he is interested in historical artefacts and pipes, and is a keen hunter who has collected trophies on expeditions across Europe and further afield.
notes: Input lists his country as Sierra Leone, but Forbes gives Slovak (and Czech) citizenship with residence in Prague, so the country field looks wrong. Very private. AGEL's press spokesperson (Radka Miloševská) is the published media route.

name: Manuel Villar
current_role: Chairman, Vista Land & Lifescapes and Villar Land Holdings; president of the Nacionalista Party
profile: Born in 1949 in Tondo, Manila, Manny Villar went from selling seafood with his mother to building the Philippines' largest homebuilder, Vista Land, now run by his son Paolo. He also controls mall operator Vistamalls, VistaREIT, AllHome, AllDay Marts and Premiere Island Power REIT, and is building the 3,500-hectare Villar City south of Manila. A former House speaker and Senate president.
interesting_fact: He started his business in 1975 delivering sand and gravel in Las Piñas with two reconditioned trucks. The firm later expanded into building and selling homes.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he was an accountant at SGV & Co. and then a financial analyst at the Private Development Corporation of the Philippines, where he sold World Bank loans. He holds a BBA (1970) and an MBA (1973) from UP Diliman.
notes: High public profile as a politician. Children Mark and Camille are senators; avoid. Premiere Island Power REIT (solar assets) is relevant to the energy theme. Vista Land and his own site blocked automated fetching, so no published press email was verified; Vista Land investor relations is the likely route. Named in Forbes Asia Heroes of Philanthropy 2024.

name: Ramesh Jaisinghani
current_role: Promoter shareholder, Polycab India (not listed among current directors on Polycab's key-people page; his son Nikhil sits on the board)
profile: One of the Jaisinghani brothers behind Polycab India, the country's largest maker of wires and cables. His older brother Inder (now chairman and MD) started it as a trading firm in 1986. Polycab supplies power, solar and optical-fibre cables to the power, oil and gas and renewables industries, added fans, LEDs and switchgear in 2014, and listed in 2019. His fortune comes from his stake.
interesting_fact: Polycab's cables go into the power, oil and gas and renewable-energy sectors, including dedicated solar cables, which makes the family an indirect play on India's grid and energy build-out.
notes: Low personal profile, with no interviews or personal channels found. Inder Jaisinghani is the public face. Research was limited because the web search budget was exhausted.
